NAHHAS:v5p19/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r21.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء وعاصم الجحدري وأبو عمرو والكسائي
NAHHAS:v5p19/r21.claim: Hasan, Abu Raja, Asim al-Jahdari, Abu Amr, and al-Kisaʾi transmit one reading of the phrase about those before Pharaoh.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r21.anchor: قراءة الحسن وأبي رجاء وعاصم الجحدري وأبي عمرو والكسائي

NAHHAS:v5p19/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r22.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن كثير والأعمش وحمزة
NAHHAS:v5p19/r22.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, al-Aʿmash, and Hamza read ومن قبله; both expressions are adverbs of time.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r22.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن كثير والأعمش وحمزة ( ومن قبله ) وهما منصوبان على الظرف

NAHHAS:v5p19/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r23.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p19/r23.claim: Hasan explains the phrase as those before Pharaoh and those with him.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r23.anchor: قال الحسن ومن قبله ومن معه

NAHHAS:v5p19/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r24.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v5p19/r24.claim: Abu Ubayd objects to ومن قبله because there were believers among Pharaoh’s people.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r24.anchor: ورد أبو عبيد على من قرأ ومن قبله لأنه قد كان فيهم مؤمنون

NAHHAS:v5p19/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r25.claim: Nahhas says Abu Ubayd’s objection is not necessary because the meaning is clarified by the reference to the overturned cities and their wrongdoing.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r25.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا لا يلزم لأنه قد عرف المعنى بقوله جل وعز

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r3.claim: They read “min maʿahum” with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning followers and troops accompanying a person; this is also reported from al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī and narrated from ʿĀṣim.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r3.anchor: ومن قبلهم بكسر القاف وفتح الباء، وهو قراءة الحسن والسلمي واختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r4.claim: The other readers say “before him,” referring to earlier peoples; the “with him” reading is supported by readings attributed to Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r4.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: ومن قبله بفتح القاف وسكون الباء، أي: من تقدمه من الأمم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r5.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the singular “the overturned city” without the alif, whereas the common reading is plural.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة: والمؤتفكات بالألف على الجمع، وعن الحسن: المؤتفكة بغير ألف

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r4.claim: Al-muʾtafikah refers to Lot’s overturned settlements, ruined by earthquake and covered by a stone-bearing wind with sand and pebbles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r4.anchor: Here, it refers to the places inhabited by the nation of Lot (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r5.claim: Quraysh could often see the remains of Lot’s settlements.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r5.anchor: The Quraysh were often able to see the remnants of these people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r6.claim: Lot’s people met the same fate as ‘Ād and Thamūd because they shared the same crime.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p450/r6.anchor: They too met a similar fate as the people of ‘ Ād and the Tham ūd since both had committed the same crime.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r10.speaker: الجمهور وأبو جعفر وشيبة والسلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r10.claim: Most readers and several authorities take min qablihi temporally, meaning earlier unbelieving nations such as Noah's people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r10.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة وأبو جعفر وشيبة والسلمي: ومن قبله، ظرف زمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p255/r11.claim: A kasra reading of qablihi is spatial, meaning Pharaoh's supporters and people in his vicinity; al-muʾtafikāt are Lot's towns, and al-khāṭiʾah means wrongful acts or error.

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r1.claim: Although the phrase is grammatically general, Rāzī says its intended scope is disbelieving peoples, not believers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r1.anchor: لفظ عام ومعناه خاص في الكفار دون المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو، عاصم، الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r2.claim: These three readers vocalize qāf with kasra and bāʾ with fatḥa in min-qablihi.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم والكسائي ، { ومن قبله } بكسر القاف وفتح الباء

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r3.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r3.claim: Sībawayh explains qabl as what lies before something; usage broadens it to what is adjacent or owed to someone, so the phrase means Pharaoh’s followers and troops.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r3.anchor: قال سيبويه : قبل لما ولي الشيء تقول : ذهب قبل السوق

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبي، أبو موسى
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy, and Abū Mūsā are reported to have read the phrase as wa-man, supporting the reading discussion.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r4.anchor: ما روي أن ابن مسعود وأبيا وأبا موسى

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r5.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r5.claim: A separate report says Ubayy alone read Mūsā wa-man maʿahu.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r5.anchor: روى عن أبي وحده أنه قرأ : { موسى ومن معه }

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r6.claim: Al-muʾtafikāt denotes the communities of Lot whom God destroyed, understood collectively.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r6.anchor: أما قوله : { والمؤتفكات } فقد تقدم تفسيرها ، وهم الذين أهلكوا من قوم لوط

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r7.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa may be a verbal noun meaning error, like al-khaṭaʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r7.anchor: فيه وجهان الأول : أن الخاطئة مصدر كالخطأ

RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, it means a sinful deed or deeds marked by grave error.
RAZI-FULL:v30p93#3/r8.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون المراد بالفعلة / أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

STUDYQURAN:69:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r1.claim: The passage shifts from the destruction of pre-Islamic Arabian disbelievers to opponents of prophets in the Judeo-Christian tradition.
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r1.anchor: These verses mark a shift from the discussion of the afflictions that befell the disbelievers from pre-Islamic Arabian tribes to those who disbelieved in prophets of the Judeo-Christian tradition

STUDYQURAN:69:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r2.claim: “Those before him” can mean the generations preceding Pharaoh.
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r2.anchor: Those before him indicates the generations before Pharaoh

STUDYQURAN:69:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r3.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r3.claim: With different voweling, wa man qibalahu can mean those who were with Pharaoh, namely his followers.
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r3.anchor: “those who were with him,” meaning those who followed Pharaoh (IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:69:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r4.speaker: R, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r4.claim: “Those subverted” most likely refers to the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah, to whom Lot was sent.
STUDYQURAN:69:9/r4.anchor: to the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah, to whom Lot had been sent as a messenger (R, Ṭ, Z)

TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r1.speaker: قراء المدينة والكوفة ومكة خلا الكسائي
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r1.claim: Most Medinan, Kufan, and Meccan readers except al-Kisāʾī read min qablahu, meaning the nations who came before Pharaoh.
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r1.anchor: قراء المدينة والكوفة ومكة خلا الكسائي: {ومن قبله} [هود: 17] بفتح القاف وسكون الباء

TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r2.speaker: قراء البصرة والكسائي
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r2.claim: The Basran readers and al-Kisāʾī read min qibilihi, meaning people from Pharaoh’s own land, the Copts, who came with him.
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r2.anchor: قراء البصرة والكسائي: (ومن قبله) بكسر القاف وفتح الباء، بمعنى: وجاء مع فرعون

TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both readings as well-known and sound in meaning, so either reading is correct.
TAB-FULL:v23p215#3/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي أنهما قراءتان معروفتان صحيحتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies al-muʾtafikāt as Lot’s town.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات} [الحاقة: 9] قرية لوط

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r2.claim: Qatāda notes a reading that says Pharaoh came with those who were with him.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات} [الحاقة: 9] قرية لوط. وفي بعض القراءة: «وجاء فرعون ومن معه»

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies al-muʾtafikāt as Lot’s people, their city, and their crops.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة} [الحاقة: 9] قال: المؤتفكات: قوم لوط، ومدينتهم وزرعهم

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that Gabriel uprooted Lot’s city, raised and overturned it, then stones followed; he cites the description of the stones in Hūd.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة} [الحاقة: 9] قال: المؤتفكات: قوم لوط، ومدينتهم وزرعهم، وفي قوله:

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd explains musawwamah as prepared for punishment.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r5.anchor: وقرأ قول الله: {حجارة من سجيل منضود مسومة} [هود: 83] قال: المسومة: المعدة للعذاب

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses those mentioned as the deniers.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة} [الحاقة: 9] يعني المكذبين

TAB-FULL:v23p217/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r7.claim: Qatāda says al-muʾtafikāt are Lot’s people, whose land was overturned.
TAB-FULL:v23p217/r7.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة {والمؤتفكات} [التوبة: 70] هم قوم لوط، ائتفكت بهم أرضهم

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r10.claim: Pharaoh is the Pharaoh of Moses; those before him are earlier peoples who denied the truth; the overturned ones are the towns and population of Lot’s people.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r10.anchor: وبمن قبله الأمم المتقدمة عليه زمانا من المكذبين

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r11.claim: Ḫāṭiʾa is a verbal noun meaning error; coming with error means missing the path of servitude.

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r1.claim: A Persian verse pictures wrathful blasts turning people to dust until even their dust leaves no trace.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r1.anchor: وعاصفات قضا ازمهب قهر وزيد شدند خاك وازان خاك نيزنيست نشان

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r2.claim: The wise should strive for a second life through enduring truthful remembrance; Abraham's prayer for a good name among later generations points to this, while true lasting life comes through divine unveiling and universal effusion.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r2.anchor: حتى يبقى في الدنيا بالعمر الثاني كما دل عليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r3.claim: The Pharaoh intended is the Pharaoh of Moses, singled out because of his extreme arrogance and self-exaltation.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r3.anchor: أي فرعون موسى أفرده بالذكر لغاية علوه واستكباره

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r4.claim: On the primary reading, man qablahu means the unbelievers who preceded Pharaoh, other than ʿĀd and Thamūd; this is a general statement after specific mention.

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب والكسائي
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, and al-Kisāʾī read qibalihi with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning Pharaoh's contemporaries among the Copts and Egyptians.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب والكسائي قبله بكسر القاف وفتح الباء بمعنى ومن معه

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r6.claim: Al-Muʾtafikāt refers to the towns of Lot, called overturned because God overturned them upon their people by sinking them.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r6.anchor: أي قرى قوم لوط أي ألها لأنها عطفت على ما قبلها من فرعون

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r7.claim: The towns are counted as five, named here Ṣaʿbah, Ṣaʿdah, ʿUmrah, Dūmā, and Sodom; Lot's people are singled out after the general grouping because their indecency was unprecedented.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r7.anchor: وهي خمس قريات صعبه وصعده وعمره ودوما سدم وهي أعظم القرى

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r8.claim: The bāʾ may indicate accompaniment or, more apparently, causation; al-khāṭiʾa can be a verbal noun meaning error or heedlessness, or an adjective for grave sinful deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r8.anchor: الباء للملابسة والتعدية وهو الأظهر أي بالخطأ أو بالغفلة أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r9.claim: On the verbal-noun reading al-khāṭiʾa is like ʿāqiba; on the other readings it modifies an omitted noun, and the preferred analysis is metaphorical attribution, as in shāʿir poetry.
BURSEVI:v10p102#2/r9.anchor: فالخاطئة على الأول مصدر كالعاقبة وعلى الأخيرين صفة لمحذوف

TABRISI:69:8-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:8-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:8-10/r10.claim: The commentary says the explanation of 'Pharaoh and those before him' has already been given.
TABRISI:69:8-10/r10.anchor: { وجاء فرعون ومن قبله } مر معناه

TABRISI:69:8-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:8-10/r11.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:69:8-10/r11.claim: Al-Muʾtafikāt are the overturned towns of Lot and, by extension, nations and communities overturned with their inhabitants.
TABRISI:69:8-10/r11.anchor: أي وجاء أهل القرى المؤتفكات أي المنقلبات بأهلها عن قتادة وهي قرى قوم لوط

TABRISI:69:8-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:8-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:8-10/r12.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means their sin of associating partners with God and unbelief; as a verbal noun it resembles khaṭaʾ and khaṭīʾa.
TABRISI:69:8-10/r12.anchor: أي بخطيئتهم التي هي الشرك والكفر فالخاطئة مصدر كالخطأ والخطيئة

TABRISI:69:8-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:8-10/r13.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:69:8-10/r13.claim: Another explanation takes it as their wrongful deeds or as the erring person responsible for them.
TABRISI:69:8-10/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه بالأفعال الخاطئة أي بالنفس الخاطئة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r1.claim: Those before Pharaoh are the earlier disbelieving peoples who disbelieved as he did.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r1.anchor: أي ومن كان قبله من الأمم الكافرة التي كفرت كما كفر هو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r2.claim: The form man is general in wording but restricted in meaning here to disbelievers, excluding believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r2.anchor: و"من" لفظه عام، ومعناه خاص في الكفار دون المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143/r3.claim: A reading pronounces qāf with kasra and bāʾ with fatḥa in qabl.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh says qabl refers to what is in front of something; its use broadened until it can mean “over you.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه: (قبل) لما ولي الشيء، تقول: "ذهب قبل السوق" و"لي قبلك حق" أي فيما يليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r2.claim: Here it means Pharaoh’s followers and those surrounding him, including his troops and adherents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى: {ومن قبله} أي من يتبعه، ويحف به من جنوده وأتباعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r3.speaker: أبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r3.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads “and those with him,” supporting the interpretation of Pharaoh’s retinue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r3.anchor: ويؤكد هذه القراءة ما روي أن في حرف أبي: "ومن معه"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r4.anchor: وأكثر قول المفسرين على هذه القراءة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as Pharaoh’s assembly and troops.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد جمعه وجنوده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r6.claim: Muqatil says they are those who were with Pharaoh, a view similar to al-Kalbi’s identification of his army.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r7.claim: Al-muʾtafikāt may refer to the overturned towns with their inhabitants, with an annexed noun omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r7.anchor: يجوز أن تكون القرى التي انقلبت بأهلها، فيكون على حذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r8.claim: Muqatil identifies them as the towns of Lot’s people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the word can refer directly to the overturned people of Lot, understood collectively as peoples, nations, or groups.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون المؤتفكات الذين أهلكوا من قوم لوط؛ على معنى: والجماعات والأمم والفرق المؤتفكات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase means the people of Lot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد قوم لوط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p143#2/r11.claim: Al-Farra, followed by Abu Ishaq, identifies them as people overturned because of their wrongdoing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r1.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means the sins they used to commit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r1.anchor: قال عطاء: يريد الخطايا التي كانوا يفعلونها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets it as associating partners with God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi says the grammarians gloss it as a great error; al-khāṭiʾa is a verbal noun like khaṭaʾ and khaṭīʾa, here meaning disbelief and denial.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r4.anchor: فالخاطئة: مصدر كالخطأ والخطيئة، وهي الكفر والتكذيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p145/r5.claim: The following phrase, “they disobeyed their Lord’s messenger,” supports the interpretation as disbelief and denial.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r6.anchor: { وجاء فرعون ومن قبله } أي: تباعه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r7.speaker: من قرأ
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r7.claim: A reading with “min qablihi” means the nations who preceded Pharaoh.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ: { ومن قبله } فمعناه: من تقدمه من الأمم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r8.claim: The “overturned towns” are the people of Lot’s settlements.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r8.anchor: { والمؤتفكات } أي: أهل قرى قوم لوط

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r9.claim: “Al-khāṭiʾa” means a grave error, namely disbelief.

QASHANI:69:9-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r1.claim: Pharaoh represents the commanding soul, those before him its faculties and helpers, and the overturned cities the spiritual faculties turned from reason toward sensory appearances.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r1.anchor: من قواها وأعوانها { والمؤتفكات } من القوى الروحانية

QASHANI:69:9-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r2.claim: The error is turning away from inward realities toward outward appearances.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r2.anchor: بالخصلة التي هي خطأ وهي المجاوزة عن البواطن إلى الظاهر

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r9.claim: Those before Pharaoh means earlier generations extending back to Noah's people; this is a generalization after the particular, with Ad and Thamud included.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r9.anchor: Ve ondan evvelkiler ta kavm-i Nûh’a kadar kurûn-i ûlâ. Burada tahsisten sonra ta‘mîm vardır.

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r10.claim: The earlier generations include Ad and Thamud as well.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r10.anchor: Zira Âd ve Semûd da evvelkilerdendir.

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r11.claim: Al-mutafikat refers to the villages of Lot's people, meaning their inhabitants; it is a specification after the generalization.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r11.anchor: Lût kavminin karyeleri ki murad ahâlisi olan kavm-i Lût’tur. Bu da ta‘mîmden sonra tahsistir.

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r12.claim: The expression's reversal and undulation vividly evoke the Haaqqa and the scenes of rebellion that caused it.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r12.anchor: İfadenin bu suretle alt üst edilerek dalgalandırılması

ELMALILI:69:9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:9/r1.claim: Khatia means an error, sin, or crime in the sense opposite to correctness rather than intention; here it is the crime of denial already mentioned.
ELMALILI:69:9/r1.anchor: “kasd” mukabili değil de “savâb” mukabili hata, hatî’e ve cinayet işlemek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r1.claim: Pharaoh here is the Egyptian king from the time of Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r1.anchor: Firavun’dan maksat, Hz. Mûsâ zamanındaki Mısır kralıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r2.claim: “Those before him” broadly includes peoples up to Pharaoh who were destroyed for rebellion, including Ad and Thamud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r2.anchor: Firavun’a kadar gelmiş geçmiş ve isyanları sebebiyle helâk olmuş kavimleri kapsamaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r3.claim: The overturned cities are identified as Sodom and Gomorrah, where Lot was sent as prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r3.anchor: Altı üstüne getirilen şehirler ise Lût aleyhisselâmın peygamber olarak gönderildiği Sodom ve Gomore olarak yorumlanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r4.claim: Each people disobeyed its own prophet and accused him of lying, so each faced a severe punishment; the singular “messenger” denotes a separate prophet for each community.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r4.anchor: 10. âyetteki “resul” kelimesinin tekil olması her bir kavme gönderilmiş olan ayrı bir peygamberi ifade eder

DAMGHANI:v1p365/r20.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r20.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r20.claim: Qabl can mean 'with him'; Pharaoh came accompanied by his troops.
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r20.anchor: قبله بكسر ففتح يعني معه قوله تعالى في سورة الحاقة وجاء فرعون ومن قبله يعني ومن معه من الجنود

DAMGHANI:v1p31/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p31/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p31/r9.claim: Muʾtafikāt illustrates ifk as turning or overturning; the source groups the two Qurʾanic uses together.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r1.claim: Qibal can mean “at/with me,” and can also mean ability or capacity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r1.anchor: بمعنى عند . يقال : ماله قبلي حق ، أي : عندي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r3.claim: In the Pharaoh passage, min qablihi means “with him.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p484/r3.anchor: بمعنى ' مع ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r2.claim: Lot’s overturned cities are called al-muʾtafikāt because they were turned upside down.

SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read the preposition with kasra and qāf open, meaning those on Pharaoh's side; Abū Mūsā's من تلقاءه supports this, while Ubayy's من تبعه is another variant.
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r1.anchor: قرأ بكسر القاف وفتح الباء أبو عمرو والكسائي، أي: ومن هو في جهته، ويؤيده قراءة أبي موسى

SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the ordinary adverbial form, meaning those who came before Pharaoh.
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r2.anchor: والباقون بالفتح والسكون على أنه ظرف، أي: ومن تقدمه

SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r3.claim: الخاطئة can be an adjective for the sinful deed or deeds, or a verbal noun like الخطأ, عافية, and كاذبة.
SAMIN-DURR:69:9/r3.anchor: بالفعلة أو الفعلات الخاطئة، وإما أن يكون مصدرا كالخطأ

ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r1.claim: The phrase has two readings: one means his followers or adherents, while the other means those who preceded him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r1.anchor: وقرئت ومن قبله فمن قال: ومن قبله فمعناه وتباعة، ومن قال

ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r2.claim: The overturned peoples were destroyed for their sins, especially the great falsehood of disbelief and denying the messengers; their name evokes the overturning of truth into falsehood.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r2.anchor: (والمؤتفكات) الذين ائتفكوا بذنوبهم، أي أهلكوا بذنوبهم التي أعظمها

ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r3.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means a grave error; the following verse's account of disobeying the messenger supports the emphasis on their grave sins and denial.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى (بالخاطئة) بالخطأ العظيم، والدليل على أن من عظيم آثامهم الكذب قوله:

ASAD-NOTES:69:9#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:9#n5/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:9#n5/r1.claim: The overthrown cities are Sodom and Gomorrah, the cities of Lot's people.
ASAD-NOTES:69:9#n5/r1.anchor: Sodom and Gomorrah, the cities of Lot's people

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r1.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبان وأبو عمرو والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r1.claim: Aban's transmission from Asim, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai read ومن قبله with fatḥa on ب; Ibn Kathir, Nafi, other Asim transmissions, Ibn Amir, and Hamza use kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم في رواية أبان وأبو عمرو والكسائي: ومن قبله* [9] بفتح الباء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r2.claim: The fatḥa reading can mean those alongside Pharaoh, supported by Ubayy's ومن معه; قبل can mean what is adjacent and follows closely.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r2.anchor: حجة من قرأ: ومن قبله* أنهم زعموا أن في قراءة أبي: وجاء فرعون ومن معه

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r3.claim: The kasra reading refers to earlier communities who disbelieved; although من قبله is general, context can restrict it to disbelievers.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r3.anchor: وحجة من قال: ومن قبله من قبله من الأمم التي كفرت كما كفر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r5.claim: Kasra on qāf with fatḥa on bāʾ means “with him/at his presence”; fatḥa on qāf and sukūn on bāʾ means those who preceded him among unbelievers.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351/r5.anchor: يقرأ بكسر القاف وفتح الباء وبفتح القاف وسكون الباء فالحجة لمن كسر القاف

NASHR:v2p389/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p389/r9.speaker: البصريان، والكسائي
NASHR:v2p389/r9.claim: The two Basrans and al-Kisāʾī read the qāf with kasra and the bāʾ with fatḥa; the others use fatḥa on qāf and silence bāʾ.
NASHR:v2p389/r9.anchor: قبله فقرأ البصريان، والكسائي بكسر القاف وفتح الباء، وقرأ الباقون بفتح القاف

QIRAAT-ER:69:9:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:6#1/r1.claim: The qibal form shifts the sense from temporal before him to spatial facing him or in his presence.
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:6#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift qabl→qibal changes meaning from ""before him"" (temporal) to ""facing him / in his presence""

QIRAAT-ER:69:9:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:10#1/r1.claim: Softening hamza to yāʾ is phonological and does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:69:9:10#1/r1.anchor: Hamzah softened to yāʾ — phonological variant without semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312#5/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the overturned cities as the people of Lot, whose land was overturned with them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ والمؤتفكات ﴾ قال هم قوم لوط ائتفكت بهم أرضوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r1.claim: “Those before him” means earlier unbelieving peoples, including Noah’s people; this general reference follows the specific mention of ʿĀd and Thamūd.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r1.anchor: ومن تقدمه من الأمم الكافرة كقوم نوح عليه السلام وفيه تعميم بعد التخصيص فإن منهم عادا وثمودا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء وطلحة والجحدري والحسن وعاصم في رواية أبان والنحويان وأبان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the phrase min qibalihi, “those on his side/in his company,” meaning his followers and adherents.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو رجاء وطلحة والجحدري والحسن بخلاف عنه وعاصم في رواية أبان والنحويان وأبان ومن قبله بكسر القاف وفتح الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r3.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r3.claim: The reading attributed to Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd, “and those with him,” supports the sense “his followers.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r3.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة أبي وابن مسعود ومن معه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r4.claim: Al-muʾtafikāt refers to Lot’s towns, meaning their inhabitants by naming the place for its people, ellipsis, or figurative attribution; the coordination requires people capable of coming.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r4.anchor: أي قرى قوم لوط عليه السلام والمراد أهلها مجازا بإطلاق المحل على الحال أو بتقدير مضاف وعلى الإسناد المجازي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan also has a singular reading, al-muʾtafikah.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن هنا والمؤتفكة على الإفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r6.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa can mean error itself, as a verbal noun on the pattern fāʿila.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r6.anchor: ﴿ بالخاطئة ﴾ أي بالخطأ على أنه مصدر على زنة فاعلة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r7.claim: It can instead mean a greatly erroneous deed or deeds, figuratively attributed to acts rather than perpetrators; the gravity reflects how deeply errant the perpetrators were.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r7.anchor: أو بالفعلة أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم على أن الإسناد مجازي وهو حقيقة لأصحابها واعتبار العظم لأنه لا يجعل الفعل خاطئا إلا إذا كان صاحبه بليغ الخطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#3/r8.claim: The form may also be a relational adjective.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r16.speaker: أهل البصرة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r16.claim: Basran readers and al-Kisaʾi read the qāf with kasra and the bāʾ with fatḥa, meaning Pharaoh and those with him among his soldiers and followers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r16.anchor: قرأ أهل البصرة والكسائي بكسر القاف وفتح الباء، أي ومن معه من جنوده وأتباعه، وقرأ الآخرون بفتح القاف وسكون الباء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r17.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r17.claim: Other readers use fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the bāʾ, meaning Pharaoh and the unbelieving peoples before him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r17.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بفتح القاف وسكون الباء، أي ومن قبله من الأمم الكافرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r18.claim: Al-Muʾtafikāt are the towns of Lot's people, with the phrase referring to their inhabitants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r18.anchor: {والمؤتفكات} أي: قرى قوم لوط، يريد: أهل المؤتفكات.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r19.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r19.claim: Another view takes the word to mean peoples overturned and destroyed for their sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r19.anchor: وقيل يريد الأمم الذين ائتفكوا بخطيئتهم، أي أهلكوا بذنوبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r20.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r20.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r20.claim: Al-khāṭiʾah means sin and disobedience, specifically associating partners with God.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r2.claim: On the standard reading, “before him” means those who preceded Pharaoh.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r3.speaker: البصريان والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r3.claim: The Basran readers and al-Kisāʾī read “ومن قبله,” meaning those with or around Pharaoh; “ومن معه” is also transmitted as support.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r3.anchor: وقرأ البصريان والكسائي { ومن قبله } أي ومن عنده من أتباعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r4.claim: The “overturned cities” are the people of Lot's towns.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r5.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa may mean error, a sinful act, or deeds characterized by error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:8-10/r5.anchor: بالخطأ أو بالفعلة، أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r4.claim: Pharaoh is the ruler who became arrogant, claimed divinity, forgot God's power, denied the Creator, and adopted naturalism.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r4.anchor: فعتى وتجبر وادعى الإلهية ناسيا هيبتنا وقدرتنا بنقمتنا وأنكر الصانع وقال بالطبائع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r5.claim: The Basrans and al-Kisāʾī read the phrase with a locative sense, covering Pharaoh’s vicinity and those following his way; the other readers give it the temporal sense “before him,” opposite “after.”
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r5.anchor: على قراءة البصريين والكسائي بكسر الكاف وفتح الموحدة , فعم ذلك كل من كان كافرا عاتيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r6.claim: The “overturned towns” are the towns of Lot, overturned with their inhabitants, then pelted with sulfur stones, sunk, and inundated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r6.anchor: وهي قرى قوم لوط عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r7.claim: “Al-khāṭiʾa” means error itself or acts that lead into wrongdoing, including Lot’s people’s sexual misconduct, shirk, and other disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r7.anchor: أي الخطأ أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ التي تتخطى منها إلى نفس الفعل القبيح من اللواط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r8.claim: Lot’s people committed unprecedented sins and suffered an unparalleled punishment; both refute natural philosophers by showing events outside ordinary nature.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p123/r8.anchor: فكان كل من فعلهم الذي لم يسبقهم به أحد من العالمين وعذابهم الذي ما كان مثله قبل ولا بعد , رادا على أهل الطبائع

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r8.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r8.claim: ʿĀṣim recited the qāf in “wa-man qablahu” with fatḥa, according to the source's description.
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r8.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله} بنصب القاف

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains “those before him” as those who were with Pharaoh.
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج {وجاء فرعون ومن قبله} قال: ومن معه

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r10.claim: Qatāda identifies the overturned settlements as Lot's people, whose land was overturned with them.
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {والمؤتفكات} قال: هم قوم لوط ائتفكت بهم أرضهم

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {بالخاطئة} قال: بالخطايا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r1.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa may be a feminine verbal noun from khaṭiʾa, “to sin”; its ending originally marked one instance but no longer limits its sense to one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r1.anchor: والخاطئة : إما مصدر بوزن فاعلة وهاؤه هاء المرة الواحدة فلما استعمل مصدرا قطع النظر عن المرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r2.claim: Alternatively, al-khāṭiʾa is an active participle meaning “the deed containing error,” with a feminine ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r2.anchor: وإما اسم فاعل خطىء وتأنيثه بتأويل : الفعلة ذات الخطء فهاؤه هاء تأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r3.claim: With either analysis, the definite form is generic: each group brought the sin deserving punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p121/r3.anchor: والتعريف فيه تعريف الجنس على كلا الوجهين ، فالمعنى : جاء كل منهم بالذنب المستحق للعقاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة وأبو جعفر وشيبة وأبو عبد الرحمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r1.claim: These readers use من قبله with fatḥa on qaf and sukūn on ba, meaning the unbelieving nations before Pharaoh; the following Noah story supports this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة وأبو جعفر وشيبة وأبو عبد الرحمن والناس: «من قبله» بفتح القاف وسكون الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وعاصم في رواية أبان والحسن وأبو رجاء والجحدري وطلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r2.claim: These authorities read من قبله with kasra on qaf and fatḥa on ba, meaning Pharaoh’s troops and followers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو والكسائي وعاصم في رواية أبان والحسن بخلاف عنه وأبو رجاء والجحدري وطلحة: «ومن قبله» ، بكسر القاف وفتح الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r3.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb’s codex reads ومن معه, supporting the sense of Pharaoh’s company.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r3.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك أن في مصحف أبي بن كعب: «وجاء فرعون ومن معه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r4.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r4.claim: Abu Musa’s reading has ومن تلقاءه, likewise pointing to those with Pharaoh.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r5.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads ومن حوله, meaning those around Pharaoh.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r6.claim: Qabl first means what is spatially adjacent, then became broadly used like near me, in my charge, or whatever is connected to me.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r6.anchor: وقبل الإنسان: ما يليه في المكان وكثر استعمالها حتى صارت بمنزلة عندي وفي ذمتي وما يليني بأي وجه وليني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r7.claim: The muʾtafikāt are the four villages of Lot’s people; the name reflects their overturning, with their tops made bottoms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r7.anchor: و: المؤتفكات قرى قوم لوط، وكانت أربعا فيما روي، وائتفكت: قلبت وصرفت عاليها سافلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r9.claim: Al-khatiʾa can modify an omitted noun, meaning the wrongful deed, or function as a verbal noun meaning error in their disbelief and disobedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r9.anchor: و «الخاطئة» : إما أن تكون صفة لمحذوف كأنه قال بالفعل الخاطئة، وإما أن يريد المصدر، أي بالخطأ في كفرهم وعصيانهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو، يعقوب، الكسائي، أبان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r2.claim: They read min qibalihi with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning those around Pharaoh among his soldiers and followers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب والكسائي وابان بكسر القاف وفتح الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r3.speaker: الباقون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r3.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on qāf and sukūn on bāʾ, meaning the unbelieving nations before Pharaoh.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r4.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r4.claim: Al-muʾtafikāt refers to the towns of Lot's people, with their inhabitants understood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r4.anchor: أحدها قرى قوم لوط والمعنى وأهل المؤتفكات قاله الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r5.claim: It refers to people overturned by their sins, chiefly the sin of lying.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أنهم الذين ائتفكوا بذنوبهم أي هلكوا بالذنوب التي معظمها الإفك وهو الكذب قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r6.claim: An alternative identifies them as Qārūn and his people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r6.anchor: والثالث أنه قارون وقومه حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p347#2/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى بالخاطئة قال ابن قتيبة أي بالذنوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r2.speaker: قراءة الكسر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r2.claim: With qāf read kasra, the phrase means Pharaoh's contemporaries, the Coptic disbelievers who followed him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r2.anchor: قرئ بكسر القاف، أي: ومن عنده في زمانه من أتباعه من كفار القبط.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r3.speaker: قراءة الفتح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r3.claim: With qāf read fatḥa, the phrase means earlier nations resembling Pharaoh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r3.anchor: وقرأ آخرون بفتحها، أي: ومن قبله من الأمم المشبهين له.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r4.claim: The overturned towns are the peoples who denied the messengers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r5.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means the wrongful deed, namely denying what God revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r5.anchor: {بالخاطئة} أي بالفعلة الخاطئة، وهي التكذيب بما أنزل الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r7.anchor: قال الربيع: {بالخاطئة} أي: بالمعصية وقال مجاهد: بالخطايا.

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r6.claim: Falsehood, sin, and disobedience are human acts.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r6.anchor: ومنها: أن الإفك والخطيئة فعل العبد، وكذلك قوله: فعصوا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r1.claim: ومن قبله can mean those with Pharaoh or those who preceded him; readings ‘with him’ and ‘in his presence’ support the first sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r1.anchor: يريد : ومن عنده من تباعه . وقرىء : ( ومن قبله ) ، أي : ومن تقدمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r2.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r2.claim: Abd Allah and Ubayy read ‘and those with him’; Abu Musa reads ‘and those in his presence.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r2.anchor: وتعضد الأولى قراءة عبد الله وأبي ( ومن معه ) وقراءة أبي موسى : ( ومن تلقاءه )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r3.claim: المؤتفكات refers to the townspeople of Lot.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r4.claim: بالخاطئة means error, or an act or acts involving grave error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p604/r4.anchor: { بالخاطئة } بالخطأ . أو بالفعلة ، أو الأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r10.claim: A reading with qaf kasra and ba fatha means Pharaoh came with his people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r10.anchor: أحدهما : ومن معه من قومه وهو تأويل من قرأ ( ومن قبله ) بكسر القاف وفتح الباء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r11.claim: A reading with qaf fatha and ba still means those who came before Pharaoh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r11.anchor: والثاني : ومن تقدمه , وهو تأويل من قرأ ( ومن قبله ) بفتح القاف وتسكين الباء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r12.claim: The word may mean those overturned by being sunk into the earth, or it may derive from afika, a lie.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r12.anchor: في المؤتفكات قولان : أحدهما : أنها المقلوبات بالخسف . الثاني : أنها الأفكات وهي الاسم من الآفكة , أي الكاذبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r13.claim: Al-khati'a means those possessing sins and errors.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r14.claim: One view identifies the people of the overturned cities as the people of Lot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r14.anchor: وفيهم قولان : أحدهما : أنهم قوم لوط .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r15.claim: Another identifies them as Qarun and his people, whom God caused to sink.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p77/r15.anchor: الثاني : قارون وقومه , لأن الله خسف بهم .

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r11.claim: Those who came before Pharaoh means those who were with him.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r11.anchor: { وجآء فرعون ومن قبله } يعني ومن معه

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r12.claim: Al-mu'tafikat refers to the deniers, namely Lot's four towns: Sodom, Amorah, Sabura, and Damura.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r12.anchor: { والمؤتفكات } يعني والمكذبات { بالخاطئة } [آية: 9] يعني قريات لوط الأربعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r1.claim: “Those before him” can mean the nations that preceded Pharaoh.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r1.anchor: ومن تقدمه من الأمم ومن قبله بصرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r2.speaker: بصري
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r2.claim: The Basran reading is taken to mean those with Pharaoh, namely his followers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r2.anchor: ومن قبله بصرى وعلى أي ومن عنده من اتباعه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r3.claim: The overturned cities are the towns of Lot, which were overturned upon their inhabitants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r3.anchor: قرى قوم لوط فهي ائتفكت أي انقلبت بهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r4.claim: “الخاطئة” means the wrongful deed or deeds marked by great error.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#5/r4.anchor: بالفعلة أو بالأفعال ذات الخطأ العظيم

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r1.claim: Abu Amr and al-Kisai read min qablihi with a kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ, meaning Pharaoh's companions and soldiers who followed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي «ومن قبله» بكسر القاف وفتح الباء أي ومن معه وتبعه من جنوده.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r2.claim: Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer the companions reading, based on the reading attributed to Abd Allah and Ubayy, min maʿahu.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r2.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم اعتبارا بقراءة عبد الله وأبي «ومن معه».

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r3.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r3.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashari reads min tilāʾihi, 'those alongside him.'

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r4.claim: The standard reading with fatḥa on qāf and a still bāʾ means those who preceded Pharaoh, past generations and nations.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r4.anchor: الباقون «قبله» بفتح القاف وسكون الباء أي ومن تقدمه من القرون الخالية والأمم الماضية.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r5.claim: Al-muʾtafikāt refers to the people of Lot's towns.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r6.speaker: الحسن والجحدري
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r6.claim: The general reading is plural al-muʾtafikāt; al-Hasan and al-Jahdari read singular al-muʾtafikah.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r6.anchor: وقراءة العامة بالألف. وقرأ الحسن والجحدري «والمؤتفكة» على التوحيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r7.claim: Qatada says the towns were called the overturned ones because they were overturned upon their people.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: إنما سميت قرى قوم لوط «مؤتفكات» لأنها ائتفكت بهم، أي انقلبت.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi names five towns: Sabʿa, Saʿra, ʿAmra, Duma, and Sodom, the largest town.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r8.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: خمس قريات: صبعة وصعرة وعمرة ودوما وسدوم وهي القرية العظمى.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r9.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means the sinful deed, namely disobedience and disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r9.anchor: { بالخاطئة } أي بالفعلة الخاطئة وهي المعصية والكفر.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r10.claim: Mujahid explains it as the sins they used to commit.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالخطايا التي كانوا يفعلونها.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r11.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r11.claim: Al-Jurjani says it means a grave error, with khāṭiʾa functioning as a verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:9/r11.anchor: وقال الجرجاني: أي بالخطأ العظيم فالخاطئة مصدر.
